claims.claim: A sync worker waiting on I/O holds its slot while using almost no CPU, so a pod runs out of free workers long before it runs out of CPU
claims.measured: I/O wait: 276 req/s, p50 915 ms, p99 932 ms at 18% CPU
claims.why: Sync Flask stalled at 18% CPU with latency of about 900 ms, which is a worker limit and not a CPU limit.

claims.claim: Go would mostly make that waiting cheaper; Go fixes concurrency because concurrency is built in
claims.measured: I/O wait: go-gin 20,235 req/s at 47% CPU and go-nethttp 18,905 req/s, vs python-flask 276 and python-flask-gthread 374
claims.why: Go handled the waiting workload about 50–70 times better than the Flask variants, using far less CPU per request.

claims.claim: With threaded workers, the same CPU gives you several times as many slots
claims.measured: I/O wait: gthread 374 req/s (p99 686 ms) vs sync 276 req/s (p99 932 ms), about 1.35x
claims.why: Threaded workers measured only about 1.35 times the sync throughput on the waiting workload, not several times.

claims.claim: Python releases the GIL while waiting, so threads work well for this load; gthread is expected to remove most of the queueing
claims.measured: I/O wait: 374 req/s, p50 678 ms, p99 686 ms at 19% CPU for a 10 ms wait
claims.why: Under gthread a 10 ms wait still had a p50 of 678 ms, so queueing stayed heavy and was not mostly removed.

claims.claim: gthread gets most of Go's concurrency benefit for free
claims.measured: I/O wait: gthread 374 req/s, p99 686 ms vs go-gin 20,235 req/s, p99 17.5 ms
claims.why: gthread reached about 2% of Go's throughput on the waiting workload, nowhere near most of its benefit.

claims.claim: gevent workers give more concurrency per pod than threads
claims.measured: I/O wait: gevent 2,956 req/s (p50 71 ms) vs gthread 374 req/s (p50 678 ms)
claims.why: gevent handled about 8 times as many waiting requests as gthread, which matches the claim's direction.

claims.claim: Async Django (ASGI) gives little gain over gthread
claims.why: Django ASGI was not benchmarked; the only async Python server measured is FastAPI, which is a different framework.

claims.claim: Go's CPU efficiency only saves money when CPU is the cost
claims.measured: CPU fib(20): go-gin 18,218 and go-nethttp 15,093 req/s vs python-flask-gthread 1,149 and python-flask 1,078
claims.why: The claim implies Go is much more CPU-efficient than Python, and the CPU test shows it about 13–17 times faster.

claims.claim: Django REST Framework serializers are often CPU-heavy, and faster JSON encoding (orjson) fixes this more cheaply than a new language
claims.why: Neither Django REST Framework nor orjson was benchmarked.
